subject: psych
source: Cambridge IGCSE Psychology (0266) syllabus for examination in 2027, 2028 and 2029 — Cambridge International; Year 11 covers Paper 2 content (topics 4–6: visual perception, motivation and needs, language development) with non-experimental research methods (7.2–7.4) and full-course revision

weeks.topic: Observations: overt and covert, participant and non-participant
objectives: Compare types of observation
Evaluate naturalistic and controlled observations

weeks.topic: Observations: behavioural categories and inter-rater reliability
objectives: Design behavioural categories
Explain event and time sampling
Assess inter-rater reliability

weeks.topic: Visual perception: key concepts
objectives: Define sensation and perception
Describe depth cues, perceptual set and visual constancies

weeks.topic: Gibson's direct theory of perception
objectives: Explain bottom-up processing and affordances
Describe optic flow and texture gradients
Evaluate the theory

weeks.topic: Core study: Gibson and Walk (1960) — the visual cliff
objectives: Describe the procedure with infants and animals
Evaluate conclusions about innate depth perception

weeks.topic: Gregory's constructivist theory of perception
objectives: Explain top-down processing and hypotheses
Evaluate the theory using illusions

weeks.topic: Core study: Haber and Levin (2001) — familiarity and perception (experiment 2)
objectives: Describe the procedure and findings
Link findings to top-down processing

weeks.topic: Visual illusions and culture
objectives: Explain the Müller-Lyer and other illusions
Explain how culture and experience affect perception

weeks.topic: Core study: Bremner et al. (2016) — culture and visual illusions (experiment 2)
objectives: Describe the cross-cultural procedure and findings
Evaluate cross-cultural research

weeks.topic: Questionnaires and interviews
objectives: Compare open and closed questions
Compare structured, semi-structured and unstructured interviews
Evaluate self-report methods

weeks.topic: Motivation and needs: key concepts
objectives: Define motivation and needs
Distinguish intrinsic and extrinsic motivation
Explain primary and secondary drives

weeks.topic: Hull's drive reduction theory of motivation
objectives: Explain homeostasis and drive reduction
Evaluate the theory

weeks.topic: Positive reinforcement in education
objectives: Explain operant conditioning and positive reinforcement
Describe token economies in classrooms

weeks.topic: Core study: Boniecki and Moore (2003) — classroom token economy
objectives: Describe the procedure and findings
Evaluate the field study

weeks.topic: Review: visual perception, observations and drive reduction
objectives: Revise perception theories and core studies
Practise Paper 2 Section A and D questions

weeks.topic: Psychodynamic motivation and marketing; Merchant et al. (2013) nostalgic advertising
objectives: Explain unconscious motives in advertising
Describe and evaluate Merchant et al. (study 3)

weeks.topic: Motivation to exercise; Calvo et al. (2010) sports persistence
objectives: Explain intrinsic motivation and self-determination in sport
Describe and evaluate Calvo et al.

weeks.topic: Case studies: features, strengths and weaknesses
objectives: Describe the in-depth nature of case studies
Evaluate generalisability and richness of data

weeks.topic: Language development: key concepts
objectives: Describe stages of language development
Define phonemes, morphemes, syntax and semantics

weeks.topic: Biological explanation of language acquisition
objectives: Explain Chomsky's language acquisition device
Describe the critical period hypothesis

weeks.topic: Core study: Senghas (1995) — sign language acquisition
objectives: Describe the Nicaraguan Sign Language study
Link findings to the critical period

weeks.topic: Learning theory of language development; Goldstein et al. (2003)
objectives: Explain imitation and reinforcement in language learning
Describe and evaluate Goldstein et al.

weeks.topic: Piaget's cognitive theory of language development
objectives: Explain schemas, assimilation and accommodation
Explain the link between cognition and language

weeks.topic: Core study: Hewitt (2022) — schemas and language
objectives: Describe the aim, procedure and findings
Evaluate the study's methodology

weeks.topic: Non-experimental methods applied: sampling, validity and ethics (Paper 2 Section D)
objectives: Plan an observation, questionnaire or case study
Evaluate it for validity, reliability and ethics

weeks.topic: Exam skills: applying psychology to novel scenarios (AO2)
objectives: Apply theories and studies to unseen stimulus material
Use precise terms in short-answer questions

weeks.topic: Mock exams: Paper 1 and Paper 2
objectives: Complete full-length mock papers under exam conditions
Use feedback to build a revision plan

weeks.topic: Review: memory and forgetting
objectives: Revise models, forgetting and the brain
Revise core studies

weeks.topic: Review: sleep and dreams
objectives: Revise theories of sleep and dreaming
Revise core studies

weeks.topic: Review: prosocial behaviour and the experimental method
objectives: Revise explanations and core studies
Practise Section D experiment questions

weeks.topic: Review: visual perception
objectives: Revise direct and constructivist theories
Revise core studies on perception and culture

weeks.topic: Review: motivation and needs
objectives: Revise drive reduction, reinforcement, marketing and exercise
Revise core studies

weeks.topic: Review: language development and non-experimental methods
objectives: Revise language theories and core studies
Practise Section D non-experimental questions

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: Paper 1 (memory, sleep, prosocial behaviour, experimental method)
objectives: Answer all four sections with good time management
Use core studies in extended responses

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: Paper 2 (perception, motivation, language, non-experimental methods)
objectives: Answer all four sections with good time management
Apply methods to novel scenarios

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: between-paper revision of core studies and key terms
objectives: Rehearse core study details between papers
Practise quick evaluation points

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: final exam window and course reflection
objectives: Complete any remaining exam papers
Reflect on next steps in IB or A Level Psychology
